name: Machinery Injury
overview: Tractors, PTO shafts, augers, and other equipment can cause crushing, amputation, or entanglement. Safety first: turn off machinery before helping.

steps.title: Turn off the machinery
steps.detail: Shut off the engine and disconnect power before approaching. Do not try to free someone from running equipment.

steps.title: Call 911
steps.detail: Machinery injuries are often serious. Call for help immediately.

steps.title: Stop bleeding
steps.detail: Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth. For severe bleeding, use a tourniquet only if trained and blood loss is life-threatening.

steps.title: Stabilize the person
steps.detail: Keep them still and calm. If a limb is trapped, wait for emergency responders unless there is immediate danger.

steps.title: Preserve amputated parts
steps.detail: Wrap in clean cloth, place in a plastic bag, and put the bag on ice. Do not put the part directly on ice.

when_to_seek_help: Call 911 for any machinery injury involving entanglement, crushing, amputation, or loss of consciousness. Do not move the person unless necessary for safety.
prevention_tips: Never wear loose clothing around PTO shafts or rotating parts.
Use guards and shields; never remove them.
Stay clear of machinery when others are operating it.
